root_cause.text: In ksmbd_tcp_new_connection(), the alloc_transport() failure path returns without decrementing the active_num_conn counter that was incremented by ksmbd_kthread_fn(), causing a permanent leak that can exhaust the max_connections limit and block all subsequent connections.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "ksmbd_kthread_fn() increments active_num_conn before calling ksmbd_tcp_new_connection() and discards the return value, so when alloc_transport() returns NULL the socket is released and -ENOMEM returned without decrementing the counter." The patch adds `if (server_conf.max_connections) atomic_dec(&active_num_conn);` in the alloc_transport() == NULL path to fix this leak.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a missing decrement of active connection count when transport allocation fails, preventing connection count leak.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional decrement of active_num_conn (if server_conf.max_connections is non-zero) in the error path when alloc_transport fails, after sock_release(client_sk).
intent_record.how: Previously, when alloc_transport failed, the active connection count was not decremented, leading to an inflated count. Now the count is decremented so that it accurately reflects the number of active connections.
